Best Local AI Models for AMD RX 9060 XT (16GB)

The RX 9060 XT 16GB has 16GB of GDDR6 at 320 GB/s. That fits dense models up to 14B at Q4, with an 8B model at est. 45 tok/s, typical error 10% and a 14B model at est. 28 tok/s. Ollama runs it through ROCm on Linux, where the 9060 XT is on its support list; its Windows ROCm list does not include the card, so on Windows Ollama uses its Vulkan backend. This page covers the 16GB card.

Last updated: November 9, 2026 · Editor: ModelFit Team

Compare with another device
Quick answer

The best local LLM for the RX 9060 XT is Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking (est. 83 tok/s, typical error 25%) on its 16GB VRAM. It uses ~8.1GB of VRAM; the RX 9060 XT handles dense models up to ~14B at Q4. A 14B model at Q4 runs at est. 28 tok/s, typical error 10%. (ModelFit, 2026)

Sizing rule: a Q4 model needs about 0.6 GB of VRAM per billion parameters for its weights, and ModelFit budgets 90% of this card's 16GB (14.4GB) for weights, context, and KV-cache. Real files often load more than that rule, so the per-size table below checks actual builds: a size fits only when the lightest Q4 build of that size in our catalog loads within 14.4GB. MoE rows, and sizes with no such build, use a typical Q4 file size. Other strong fits: Gemma 4 12B (12B, ~8GB) and NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B (4B, ~7.9GB). On this card Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking runs at est. 83 tok/s, typical error 25%. What it will not run: a 32B model does not fit in VRAM alone, so it spills to system RAM over PCIe and slows sharply.

ModelFit estimates, not measured benchmarks: decode speed of a generic Q4_K_M model of each size at 4K context on the RX 9060 XT's 320 GB/s bandwidth. MoE rows scale by active parameters (decode reads only the active experts), so a 35B MoE runs far faster than a dense 32B. "CPU offload" sizes exceed the 16GB VRAM; dense models slow to a crawl there, MoE models degrade less because hot experts stay GPU-resident. Offload rows are rough estimates: no measured run covers offload, so they carry no typical error. What typical error means.

Fig. 2

Context costs VRAM too.

Mellum2.1 12B-A2.5B Thinking loads ~8.1 GB of weights; at 16k context the KV cache adds ~0.2 GB (still fits the ~14 GB usable VRAM), and at 64k it adds ~0.9 GB (still fits).

Weights 8.1 GBKV cache · 16k context 0.2 GBHeadroom 6.1 GBRuntime reserve 1.6 GB

The model leaves about 6.1 GB of the usable VRAM budget free after weights and 16k context.

KV-cache figures assume an fp16 cache, the llama.cpp/Ollama default. Standard GQA models use a size-class estimate (8 KV heads x 128 head dim class); hybrid linear-attention models (Qwen3.5/3.6, Qwen3-Next) use the exact per-token cost from their published config, since only their sparse full-attention layers cache KV. A q8_0 KV cache roughly halves either figure. Estimates, not measurements.

RX 9060 XT VRAM for AI: what actually fits?

ModelFit budgets about 14.4GB of the 16GB for weights and context: 14B models at Q4 (~11GB) fit with room for context, and 20B-class mixture-of-experts models load too. Bandwidth is the trade-off: 320 GB/s sits near the RTX 4060 Ti 16GB (288 GB/s) and at half the RX 9070 XT (640 GB/s, est. 79 tok/s, typical error 10% on 8B). Dense 27B and 32B models spill into system RAM.

RX 9060 XT FAQ: common questions

Does Ollama support the RX 9060 XT?

Yes. On Linux, Ollama lists the RX 9060 XT among its ROCm cards and needs the AMD ROCm v7 driver. Its Windows ROCm list does not include the card, so on Windows Ollama runs it through its Vulkan backend.

How much VRAM does the RX 9060 XT 16GB have for LLMs?

It has 16GB of GDDR6 at up to 320 GB/s (AMD specifications). ModelFit budgets about 14.4GB of it for weights and context, enough for dense models up to 14B at Q4 quantization.

RX 9060 XT vs RTX 5060 Ti 16GB for local AI?

Both have 16GB, so they hold the same models. The RTX 5060 Ti streams 448 GB/s against 320 GB/s and runs CUDA, so it is 51% faster on 8B models (est. 68 tok/s, typical error 5% vs est. 45 tok/s, typical error 10%). The 9060 XT runs Ollama and llama.cpp through ROCm or Vulkan.

RX 9060 XT vs RX 9070 XT for local LLMs?

Both have 16GB. The 9070 XT has twice the bandwidth (640 vs 320 GB/s), so it decodes faster on every model both hold: est. 79 tok/s, typical error 10% against est. 45 tok/s on 8B.

How fast is a 27B-class model on the RX 9060 XT?

The RX 9060 XT's 16GB of VRAM cannot fit a 32B model comfortably. The largest size class it fits is 20B MoE (3.6B active), at est. 59 tok/s, typical error 25%. The largest individual model in the catalog that fits is LFM2 24B-A2B Instruct (24B).
